transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. I'm here because I've been struggling with severe sleep problems and feeling extremely stressed for the past three weeks. It has gotten to the point where I just can't get any proper rest, and it's really wearing me down.
Did a specific stressful event or major change happen in your life around three weeks ago when these symptoms started?

Yes, a very stressful event did happen about three weeks ago, right when these sleep issues started. But to be honest, I find it extremely difficult to even think or talk about it, and I've realized my memory of what actually happened is really blurry and incomplete.
Even though your memory is blurry, do you experience distressing nightmares, sudden flashbacks, or unwanted memories of the event popping into your mind?

Yes, I've been having terrible, distressing nightmares that constantly wake me up and completely ruin my sleep. I don't really experience sudden flashbacks or unwanted memories popping up during the day, but the nightmares at night are truly awful.
Without sharing too many painful details, did this stressful event involve actual or threatened death, serious injury, or a threat to your physical safety?

It was an incredibly terrifying and overwhelming experience that has left me deeply shaken. However, it is still very hard for me to think or talk about it, so I can't really say more about the details of what happened.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid certain places, people, conversations, or activities that might remind you of the event?

Yes, I've been doing everything I can to avoid the place where it happened and staying away from anyone who might want to talk about it. Just being near anything that reminds me of it brings back too much distress. I feel like I have to avoid those reminders entirely just to get through the day.
Since the event happened, have you been feeling unusually jumpy, easily startled, or constantly on guard?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled. I also don't really feel like I'm constantly on guard.
Since the event, have you found it difficult to experience positive emotions, such as feeling happy, joyful, or close to others?
I haven't really noticed any change in that, to be honest. I'm not quite sure if my ability to feel happy or close to others has actually shifted.
Since the event, have you felt detached from your own body or mind, or has the world around you felt strange, dream-like, or unreal?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't feel detached from my own body or mind, and the world around me still feels completely real.

Since the event, have you had any difficulty concentrating, focusing on tasks, or keeping your mind on what you are doing?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant issues with my concentration or focus since the event. I've been able to keep my mind on my tasks and get things done without much trouble.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports experiencing a highly traumatic event three weeks ago, presenting with characteristic symptoms such as distressing nightmares, dissociative amnesia (blurry memory of the event), avoidance of trauma-related reminders, and severe sleep disturbance. Because the duration of these symptoms is currently three weeks (less than the one month required for a diagnosis of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder), Acute Stress Disorder is the most accurate diagnosis.
